question.text: Aravalli Offshore Fund (Cat II feeder from Mauritius) has appointed a domestic Investment Advisor in India to source deals. Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Advisor and the Investment Manager?

answer.text: The Investment Advisor has binding authority to execute trades on behalf of the AIF
The Advisor and the Manager must be the same entity for Cat II feeders

The Investment Advisor provides non-binding advice on investment opportunities; the Investment Manager may choose to execute or leave the same, and the Advisor is paid advisory fees BY THE INVESTMENT MANAGER (not the AIF directly)
Advisor fees are charged directly to the LPs as a fund-level expense pass-through

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, offshore funds may seek domestic investment advisory services. The advice from a domestic Investment Advisor is non-binding — the Investment Manager may choose to execute or leave it — and advisory fees are paid by the Investment Manager, not directly by the AIF or its LPs. The Trap: The binding-authority option inverts the non-binding nature of the relationship. The same-entity option invents a rule that does not appear in the source. The LP pass-through option mis-routes the fee burden; advisory fees flow through the Manager's economics. Note: Distinguish the AIF Investment Advisor (offshore-fund context, paid by the Manager) from a SEBI-registered Investment Adviser under the IA Regulations, which is a different regime.
